bug_semantics: The public GraphQL Query.order resolver accepts an attacker-controlled order UUID and loads the matching order without authenticating the caller or constraining the query to the caller's customer/session identity. An unauthenticated caller who obtains a valid UUID can therefore traverse the returned Order fields and nested resolvers to read customer email/name, billing and shipping addresses, purchased items, totals, payment state, and shipment data belonging to another customer.
flaw_origin: Commit 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e changed the order lookup from an integer order_id plus tokenPayload-derived customer_id/sid ownership predicates to a string UUID lookup alone: it deleted extraction of customerId and sid and deleted both ownership/session constraints, leaving query.where('uuid', '=', id). Later commits renamed the argument to uuid, moved the file, and replaced the base select helper, but preserved this authorization omission.
ai_marker: absent — git cat-file -p 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e shows author and committer both as The Nguyen <6950941+treoden@users.noreply.github.com>; the commit message is exactly 'Authentication and setting module' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, bot, or other attribution trailer.
evidence: The assigned GitHub advisory GHSA-c73g-mx2w-cc93 / CVE-2025-12919 identifies src/modules/oms/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js, declares @evershop/evershop <= 2.1.0 vulnerable, and supplies no first_patched_version.

The linked public disclosure https://github.com/ictrun/Evershop-Order-leak/blob/main/README.md documents an unauthenticated POST to /api/graphql with order(uuid: $uuid) returning order/customer PII; its quoted vulnerable resolver performs getOrdersBaseQuery(), where uuid equals caller input, and load(pool), with no authorization predicate.

numactl git log 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e -L 8,18:packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js traces the causal lines from the secure introduction in 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa through 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e. The latter is the first commit to delete `const { customerId, sid } = tokenPayload`, `andWhere('customer_id', '=', customerId)`, and `.or('sid', '=', sid)`, while adding the UUID-only predicate.

Direct tree comparison `git diff b398f43d4d2eedf39abf9e3658820941cbd4babd 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e -- packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.{graphql,resolvers.js}` proves immediate-parent absence: the parent requires order_id plus customer_id or sid, whereas the BIC changes the schema argument from Int to String and leaves only `query.where('uuid', '=', id)`.

The BIC is a single-parent public commit (parent b398f43d4d2eedf39abf9e3658820941cbd4babd), not a merge, move, refactor, revert, or release commit. Although it is a broad 195-file change, the public graph exposes no smaller member commit; the vulnerable authorization deletion is directly present in its own diff, so there are no decomposed SHAs.

History checks corroborate the selection: `git log -S "query.andWhere('customer_id'" -- **/Order/Order.resolvers.js` and `git log -S "customerId, sid"` identify only the secure introduction 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa and removal 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e. Blame was used only as a lead; later commits 72d478a748e7994b46f7aecee9a849a9ef15db43 and 7a7fb5b089663bf86e47d8825ca64bb7fafce2b3 merely rename/restructure the already-unscoped lookup.

Version-boundary checks show `git tag --contains 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e` includes the first tagged release 1.0.0-rc.9, v1.0.0, every listed stable release through the advisory boundary v2.1.0, and later tags v2.1.1, v2.1.2, and v2.2.1. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` also succeeds for v2.1.0, so the BIC predates and is contained in the affected range.

No fix exists in reachable history. At both v2.1.0 (70a786fadcbd55f1641f0088189da4cfe44aa79c) and the latest reachable tag v2.2.1 (abfdabcacfc49ad0df1f262c34bc46af721f2537), packages/evershop/src/modules/oms/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js still resolves order(uuid) by getOrdersBaseQuery(), adds only `where('uuid', '=', uuid)`, and returns the loaded order. The later anonymous tracking-token page code does not constrain the public GraphQL resolver itself.

BIC-only AI inspection used the raw commit object, not PR text, branch names, later code, or a fix: `git cat-file -p 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e` shows a human GitHub noreply author/committer, identical timestamps/identity, and no trailers or bot marker. This supports NOT_AI independently of any later repository activity.
reasoning: The vulnerability began as an authorization regression, not with the original GraphQL endpoint. Commit 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa initially loaded an order only when its numeric ID matched and either customer_id matched tokenPayload.customerId or sid matched tokenPayload.sid. The immediate parent of the selected BIC still has those constraints. Commit 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e deliberately converted the public argument to a string UUID and simultaneously removed both identity predicates, making possession of an order UUID sufficient. That exact removal is the smallest causally relevant public commit; subsequent parameter renames, module moves, ESM/TypeScript conversions, and query-helper refactors preserve rather than originate the flaw. The BIC predates 1.0.0-rc.9 and is an ancestor of the advisory's upper affected boundary v2.1.0. The advisory reports no patched version, and direct inspection shows the same unscoped resolver still present at v2.2.1, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are justified nulls rather than missing research. Finally, the only admissible AI evidence is the BIC commit object: it has a human author/committer and no AI/co-author/generated/bot trailer. Therefore the causal BIC is real and parent-verified, but has no commit-object AI signal, yielding NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: The vulnerability remains unpatched in the reachable public history: there is no fix commit, direct-fix commit, or first patched version to record, and the latest inspected release v2.2.1 still exposes the UUID-only resolver.
